LEARN IN A MINUTE. ARGUE FOR HOURS.

A kingdom is a connection.

No turns. Each piece has its own cooldown. Your army moves, fights and claims territory while the other army does the same.

01 / TAKE THE BOARD

Drag a piece or click it, then a destination. It automatically takes legal chess-like hops. Pieces fight nearby enemies when idle. A commanded strike charges an enemy on a legal hop; a ready defender can counterstrike. Landing requires the square to be empty.

02 / KEEP IT CONNECTED

Only orthogonally connected territory leading to your Crown earns Ink and powers Bells. Sowers claim a cross on landing. Wells boost income. Disconnected territory dims.

03 / FOLD THE WORLD

Keep a Weaver alive. Own 3 supplied squares on a plate, spend 26 Ink, and rotate all nine squares 90 degrees. Units, territory and the two off-center flank Bells ride along. The central Bell stays at its pivot. No one gets to veto your geography.

04 / BORROW THE PAST

Echo spends 32 Ink to return a selected living piece to its position six seconds ago and restore at least its old health. The remembered square must be empty. Territory does not rewind. Dead pieces stay dead.

05 / WIN TWO WAYS

Destroy the enemy Crown, or keep all three Bells connected to yours for 20 uninterrupted seconds. At the time limit, kingdom score breaks the tie: supplied squares + 35 per Bell + half Crown HP + 0.12 per other piece HP.

06 / THE BOARD HAS IDEAS

Every 35 seconds, an announced middle plate rotates. The final minute increases damage by 30%. Victory is about timing, not just clicking faster.

Controls

1-5 recruit · Q fold · E echo · X stop · C cycle pieces · F select Crown · Arrows + Enter order · Shift-click queue · Space pause solo · Esc cancel · Right-drag orbit · Scroll zoom
JUST YOU. YOUR FRIEND. A VERY BAD IDEA.

A private table.

Both players must open the same running CROWNFOLD server. No accounts, public lobby, or matchmaking.

OR JOIN YOUR FRIEND

On your own computer: npm start. For a trusted LAN, start with --lan and share the server's local-network address. Never expose the plain-HTTP server directly to the internet.
